newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore says reviews Waterford merger move.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore says reviews Waterford merger move.

text.p: Ireland's Avonmore Foods Plc said on Monday it regretted Waterford Foods Plc's rejection of its recent merger proposal and was now seeking to determine if a realistic basis exists for further merger discussions.
Avonmore launched a 281 million Irish pound offer for Waterford Foods in early April in a bid to create Ireland's biggest food group with a combined turnover of 2.5 billion.
Waterford responded to the "friendly" merger proposal on May 2 saying it could not endorse Avonmore's offer as it did not reflect the company's underlying value or strategic position.
Avonmore said on Monday it regretted Waterford's decision and continued to believe that a merger "...is in the best interests of the shareholders and milk suppliers in both organisations".
"Avonmore will now seek to determine whether a realistic basis exists for merger discussions between the two parties," Avonmore said in a statement after a regular board meeting on Monday.
The offer must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op, which owns 68 percent of the Plc's shares, and Waterford Foods shareholders.

Avonmore says the food sector is facing enormous changes which could hit the incomes and livelihoods of Waterford's supplier farmers. It says further consolidation is needed in the Irish dairy industry and that the merger with Waterford would be in the best interests of shareholders and milk suppliers for both organisations.
Under the terms of the merger proposal, Avonmore has offered one Avonmore share for every two Waterford Foods Plc and Waterford Co-op Ltd ordinary shares.
